title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
notes: A brilliant pick if you enjoy detective novels. It's a true mystery — you never know what's coming next, and it keeps you hooked from start to finish. You just don't want to put it down.

title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
author: Robert Kiyosaki
notes: The core idea is distinguishing assets from liabilities: buy things that put money in your pocket and avoid things that take money out. It also covers understanding taxes, learning what you are good at, and delegating rather than doing everything yourself.

title: The Richest Man in Babylon
author: George S. Clason
notes: Teaches practical principles for managing money: pay yourself first, invest wisely, and work hard and consistently to build wealth over time.

title: Who Not How
author: Dan Sullivan & Benjamin Hardy
notes: Focuses on finding the right people to work with rather than trying to do everything yourself. It teaches how to build a strong team, identify what the team is missing, and lead effectively by delegating to the right who instead of figuring out the how alone.

title: Eat That Frog
author: Brian Tracy
notes: A productivity book offering 21 ways to stop procrastinating and get the most important things done first.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
notes: Explains how small, consistent habits compound into major change over time, and lays out a clear framework for building good habits and breaking bad ones.

title: Mehrobdan Chayon
author: Abdulla Qodiriy
notes: An engaging historical novel that vividly portrays life in that era.

author: George Orwell
notes: A well-written book. Some parts feel boring, but it gets exciting quickly. It clearly shows how a government can control people and keep them obedient and loyal to the state.
